newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says natgas output up despite Cactus blast.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says natgas output up despite Cactus blast.

text.p: Mexico's state owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Tuesday that natural gas output in the first eight months of the year rose 7.6 percent over the same period a year earlier to record an average daily volume of 3.332 billion cubic feet per day (cfd).
The increase comes despite the problems Pemex has suffered following the July explosion at its Cactus natural gas processing plant, which hit production.

In the January-August reference period, Pemex obtained an average daily output of 458,000 barrels per day (bpd) of condensed liquids, such as ethane, liquid gas and gasolines, up 1.1 percent over the same period a year earlier.

For liquid gas, Pemex produced an average of 209,000, up 1.9 percent over the same period in 1995. For ethane, output was up 1.2 percent over the first eight months of last year at an average 85,000 bpd in the period.
Pemex said 85,000 bpd of gaslines were produced in the period, but did not give a precise percentage change, just adding that it was "a smiliar quantity compared to the same period a year earlier."

Pemex proceses natural gas and condensed liquids at its centers in Nuevo Pemex, Ciudad Pemex and La Venta in Tabasco state, Cactus in Chiapas state, Reynosa in Tamaulipas state and also in La Cangrejera, Matapionche, Morelos, Pajaritos and Poza Rica in Veracruz state.
Pemex made no mention of the Cactus blast in its statement.

"Pemex Gas and Basic Petrochemicals is sticking to its programme orientated to imporving the operating efficiency of its gas and condensed liquids processing in its work stations to take advantage of the country's gas output.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
